## State-request queue, game+5D8h

The queue is an MSVC `std::deque<int>`. The producer 004d3ed0 allocates a block with a 10h-byte
`malloc` at 004d3f13 and the drain indexes it as `map[off / 4][off % 4]`, so `DEQUESIZ` is
`10h / sizeof(int)` = 4. Fields relative to game+5D8h:

| Offset | Field |
| --- | --- |
| +0h (game+5D8h) | allocator slot, untouched by push_back and pop_front |
| +4h (game+5DCh) | block map, `int**`; a null slot is an unallocated block |
| +8h (game+5E0h) | block count |
| +Ch (game+5E4h) | head offset, in elements |
| +10h (game+5E8h) | element count |

Block index for an offset: `off / 4`, minus the block count once when it is not smaller
(004e4486 and 004d3eff). One subtraction suffices because neither caller lets the offset reach
two map lengths.

`enqueue` (004d3ed0, `RET 4`) takes a **pointer** to the value (004d3f35 loads through it), so
call sites that look like they push a literal are pushing the address of a stack slot. It grows
when `(head + count) % 4 == 0` and the block count is not greater than `(count + 4) / 4`, and
allocates the target block lazily. The existing ledger record for 004d3ed0 describes the element
as 10h bytes; 10h is the block size and the element is a 4-byte `int`. That address is outside
this packet's lease, so the correction is recorded here rather than applied.

`grow` (004d20d0) enlarges the map by `max(count, max(block_count / 2, 8))` and rotates the
blocks so the sequence starting at the head block stays contiguous, leaving the new slots behind
it. 004d2211 adds only to the block count: **the head offset is not adjusted**, unlike the usual

**State 2 to state 4.** `BSP_Game_RequestState` (004d7920) is a one-line wrapper over
`BSP_Game_EnqueueStateRequest`. Of its 28 call sites, exactly two push 4: 0068d8bc in
`BSP_TitleScreen_Skip` and 0068d90e in `BSP_TitleScreen_Advance`, which is slot `+4h` of the title
vtable `00CF7A98`. Both are guarded by `game+5E8h == 0` (nothing already queued) and both then
clear `game+5ECh`. `GGame::OnInitTitle` calls the virtual normally and calls
`BSP_TitleScreen_Skip` instead when `skipTitle` is set.

normal_stack.qualification: Syntactic normal-return paths, not feasibility or unwind proof. All seven CALL sites are external capsules with callee argument pop zero; REP instructions are symbolic ECX/DF-dependent memory operations with no stack change. The xlen frontier is allowed to return only hypothetically; its behavior and volatile outputs are unresolved. No per-iteration REP expansion or Native execution.

field_contract.role: Current map reloaded after allocation, before prefix moves, before split remainder, and before free. Updated only at 004D221B after free and capacity update.
Capacity read before limit/growth decision, reloaded after allocation for suffix span, then current value receives ADD at 004D2211. It is not assigned captured B0+R.
Head offset read once at 004D2113, unsigned shifted by two before allocator; no explicit write.
No explicit read or write of queue count in this body.

growth_policy.guard: Unsigned compare u32(M-B0) >= incoming R0 skips 004CFE20; if false the named xlen frontier is called, with no fresh throw/no-return/exception-type proof.
growth_policy.preferred: I=max(8, B0>>1) on the admitted path. Promote R0 to I only when R0<I and unsigned B0<=u32(M-I). Otherwise retain R0. Promotion writes the actual incoming stack argument at entry ESP+4.

well_formed_admitted_example.qualification: Arithmetic illustration only; no allocation or synthetic execution.

growth_policy.failure_frontier_return: If 004CFE20 returns, EAX and EDX are not restored: later arithmetic consumes its volatile outputs. Do not replace this with a fabricated returning error or assume the normal admitted formula.
growth_policy.source_gap: Current C++ always promotes count to max(8, blocks.size()/2) and has no corresponding native maximum guard/failure provider.

allocation_boundary.inputs: ECX=u32(current EAX + effective EDX), EDX=0; no stack arguments. Admitted unmodified path uses B0+R. EBX retains queue; EBP retains head>>2.
allocation_boundary.output: EAX is saved at entry ESP-8 and used as new map base. No local null test.
allocation_boundary.limits: Element scaling, allocation failure behavior, overflow handling, initialization, matching release and allocator ABI are unopened. Register count is not proof of a provider byte count or new[] implementation.

move_contract.stack_arguments: Each 00BF67A7 site pushes count, source, destination_size, destination, then caller discards 16 bytes. At all four sites destination_size equals count; EAX return codes are not tested.

suffix.range: H=unsigned head>>2 captured before allocation. After allocation M1=current map, B1=current capacity. L1=s32(u32(4*B1-4*H))>>2; N1=u32(4*L1). D is allocator output. T1=u32(D+4*H+N1). Copy(D+4*H,N1,M1+4*H,N1) iff L1!=0; T1 saved at entry ESP-4 and reloaded after call while args are still live.

move_contract.increment: R is reloaded from the incoming entry ESP+4 slot at 004D2165 after optional suffix copy, not held from allocation. Branch uses unsigned H>R.

large_increment.prefix: At 004D216D reload current M2; Lh=s32(u32(4*H))>>2. Copy(T1,u32(4*Lh),M2,u32(4*Lh)) iff Lh!=0.
large_increment.zero: 004D2195 writes R-H zero DWORDs starting at T1+4*Lh when R-H!=0. Then 004D2197 reloads current argument R. If H!=0, shared 004D21FB writes H zero DWORDs from saved D and 004D21FD reloads current argument R.

small_increment.prefix: 004D21A7 reloads current M2. Lr=s32(u32(4*R))>>2. Copy(T1,u32(4*Lr),M2,u32(4*Lr)) at 004D21C0 iff Lr!=0.
small_increment.remainder: 004D21C8 reloads current M3 even after the preceding copy. L2=s32(u32(4*H-4*R))>>2; N2=u32(4*L2). Copy(saved D,N2,M3+4*R,N2) at 004D21E9 iff L2!=0. If R!=0, shared 004D21FB writes R zero DWORDs from saved D+N2, then reloads argument R.

stable_valid_interpretation.preconditions: Valid nonoverlapping queue/stack/new-map storage, B0/B1/map and R stable across providers, valid head/capacity ranges, successful providers, normal preserved nonvolatile registers, DF clear at each REP.
stable_valid_interpretation.large: Copy old[H,B) to new[H,B), old[0,H) to new[B,B+H); zero new[B+H,B+R) and new[0,H).
stable_valid_interpretation.small: Copy old[H,B) to new[H,B), old[0,R) to new[B,B+R), old[R,H) to new[0,H-R); zero new[H-R,H).
stable_valid_interpretation.limits: These map-entry rotations do not override the actual wrapping 32-bit arithmetic, signed shifts, reloads or provider boundaries. Pointed 16-byte element blocks are not locally copied.

move_contract.REP: No CLD occurs in the body. At each REP STOSD, ECX is the unsigned repetition count, EAX is zero and EDI advances/decrements by four according to DF; forward ranges above require DF=0. Faults/partial writes/invalid counts are not repaired locally.

order: 004D2204/2206 test and skip free only if current map is zero
004D2209 call 00BF65AC with current map, while it remains published
004D220E discard four-byte free argument (missing from Ghidra listing, present in verified bytes)
004D2211 add held EDI increment to CURRENT queue capacity
004D2214 reload saved new-map stack slot at entry ESP-8
004D221B publish reloaded pointer as queue map
final_publication.observability: Free can observe the old map still published. Capacity is updated before the replacement pointer. Reloaded current old map/capacity can differ from allocation/copy inputs after reentry. Saved new pointer and incoming argument remain stack memory; alias writes are not assumed impossible by the body.
final_publication.normal_results: EDX is the late loaded new-map value; EAX is zero if free skipped, otherwise unprescribed free-call output. No semantic return value/type inferred.

failure_and_alias_limits: No local allocation-null guard, provider-result check, rollback or exception cleanup established.
No provider body, allocator family, maximum throw type, CRT failure-handler behavior or unwind behavior is newly analyzed.
Malformed head/capacity, unsigned overflow, signed SAR spans and DF changes are not normalized to safe STL ranges.
The four memmove_s call sites use equal size/count but unchecked return values; they cannot be silently replaced with success-only value loops.
Input queue identity is retained in EBX. No current-game or callback publication is explicitly read; named fields can still alias provider-visible memory.
No explicit head/count write or pointed-block clear occurs. Provider/alias effects are not excluded.

ABI.receiver: Entry ECX is captured as queue in EBX.
ABI.argument: One stack DWORD at entry ESP+4; the routine can rewrite it with promoted increment and rereads it after providers/REP operations.
ABI.cleanup: RET 4 establishes the growth callee cleanup previously assumed by 004D3ED0. Four saved registers and eight local bytes are balanced on every normal path under stated callee capsules.
ABI.prototype: Live undefined FUN_004d20d0(void) is not the recovered register/stack ABI. No Ghidra signature or listing edits.
